resources.string: Voltwise keeps at most 100,000 readings and 10,000 sessions on this phone; the oldest go first. The retention setting can remove them sooner.\n\nClearing deletes readings, sessions and app statistics. Your settings and the current calibration stay. Android\'s own battery statistics are not affected.

JSON keeps everything in one file, with units and UTC times spelled out. CSV writes one file per table into a folder you choose.

The period ends when the export starts. Sessions that overlap it are exported whole, not cut at its edges.

Exports show when and how you use your phone. Share them only with people you choose.

Imports add to your history and never start monitoring. Identical records are skipped. A file that conflicts with what is stored, or has an invalid record, is refused as a whole, so nothing is half imported.\n\nA CSV file holds readings or sessions; import them one file at a time. Per-app usage from older exports is not imported, and Voltwise rebuilds it from new sessions. Files up to 64 MiB are accepted.
Readings added: %1$s · sessions added: %2$s · extended: %3$s · unchanged: %4$s

The backup holds your settings, including the current unit and sign overrides. It never contains battery history or the calibration Voltwise detected on this phone.\n\nA restore checks the whole file first. If anything in it is wrong, no setting changes.
Settings restored · applied: %1$s · skipped: %2$s · not applied: %3$s
Deletes readings, sessions and app statistics. Settings and calibration stay.
This stops monitoring and permanently deletes every reading, session and app statistic. Your settings and the current calibration stay.\n\nSave an export first if you want a copy.
